title: Generation of Human Blood Vessel Organoids from Pluripotent Stem Cells
protocol: Mix 40 mL of knock-out DMEM/F12 (low osmolality medium without L-glutamine or HEPES buffer optimized for human ESC and iPSC growth) with 10 mL of knock-out serum replacer (KOSR), 0.5 mL of 200 mM L-alanyl-L-glutamine dipeptide in 0.85% NaCl, 0.5 mL of non-essential amino acids (NEAA), and 35 µL of beta-mercaptoethanol to prepare the aggregation medium.
Mix 25 mL of DMEM/F12 with 25 mL of neurobasal media, 1 mL of B27 supplement, 0.5 mL of N2 supplement, and 35 µL of beta-mercaptoethanol to prepare N2B27 (N2 and B27 supplemented basic medium).
Supplement N2B27 medium with ChiR (12 µM) and BMP-4 (30 ng/mL) to prepare the mesoderm induction medium.
Supplement N2B27 medium with VEGFA (100 ng/mL) and forskolin (2 µM).

Mix 5.627 mL of 0.1 N NaOH, 2.498 mL of 10x DMEM, 473 μL of HEPES, 368 μL of 7.5% sodium bicarbonate, 233 μL of 200 mM L-alanyl-L-glutamine dipeptide in 0.85% NaCl, and 3.451 mL of Ham's F-12 to prepare the basic matrix solution.

Mix 500 μL of purified bovine collagen type I with 250 μL of solubilized basement membrane matrix secreted by Engelbreth-Holm-Swarm mouse sarcoma cells and 250 μL of prepared basic matrix solution to create 1 mL of ECM solution.
Use 0.5 mL of ECM solution for a bottom layer in each well of the plate.
Add remaining 0.5 mL plus aggregates for the top layer in each well of the plate.
Formulate 50 mL of flexible serum-free medium (SFM) for hematopoietic cell development.
Add 1.3 mL aliquot of the flexible SFM nutrient supplement to the medium.
Mix 15% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 250 µL of penicillin-streptomycin, and 500 µL of L-alanyl-L-glutamine dipeptide in 0.85% NaCl into the SFM.
Add VEGFA at a concentration of 100 ng/mL to the medium.
Add FGF2 at a concentration of 100 ng/mL to the medium.
Mix 0.5 g of bovine serum albumin, 1.5 mL of fetal bovine serum, 250 µL of Tween 20, and 250 µL of Triton X-100 in a solution.
Add 500 µL of sodium deoxycholate (1% wt/vol stock) to the mixture.
Mix 47.5 mL of 1x phosphate-buffered saline into the buffer solution.
Pipette up and down until all components are well incorporated and the solution is clear.
Perform cell culture using LDEV-free reduced growth factor basement membrane matrix-coated 6-well tissue culture plates with stem cell culture medium.
Passage cells once they reach ~70% confluency using mammalian cell dissociating enzyme for 3-4 min at 37°C.
Aspirate the culture medium from two wells of a 6-well cell culture plate.
Replace the aspirated medium with 1 mL of cell dissociation reagent and incubate for 5 min at 37°C.
Prepare the necessary volume of aggregation medium in a 15 mL conical tube as needed.
Aspirate the 1 mL of cell dissociation reagent.
Suspend the cells in 1 mL of aggregation medium.
Create a single-cell suspension with gentle up-down pipetting prior to counting.
Count cells using an automated cell counting device or a standardized system under a microscope.
Calculate the number of cells needed for the experiment.
Add the appropriate volume of cell suspension to the aggregation medium in a 15 mL high-clarity polypropylene conical tube.
Gently pipette the diluted cell suspension up and down to ensure homogenous distribution.
Pipette 3 mL of the diluted cell suspension into each well of a 6-well ultra-low attachment culture plate.
Place the plate in an incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and greater than 90% humidity.
Set up one 15 mL high-clarity polypropylene conical tube per well of the 6-well ultra-low attachment culture plate.
Use a circular motion to gather the aggregates in the center of each well.
Gently collect the aggregates and surrounding medium from each well using a 1 mL pipette.
Place the collected material into their corresponding 15 mL high-clarity polypropylene conical tubes.
Allow the aggregates to sediment at room temperature for 1 hour.
Aspirate the supernatant with caution once the hour has passed, ensuring the aggregates remain undisturbed.
Resuspend the aggregates in each tube in 2 mL of mesoderm induction medium.
Place the resuspended aggregates back into their respective wells on a 6-well ultra-low attachment culture plate.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C until day 4.
Gently pipette each well up and down once per day to maintain similar aggregate sizes if they attach or grow together.
Collect the aggregates on day 4 and allow them to settle before changing the medium to vascular induction medium.
Set up one 15 mL conical tube per well of the 6-well ultra-low attachment culture plate.
Use a circular motion to gather aggregates in the center of each well.
Gently collect aggregates and surrounding medium from each well using a 1 mL pipette.
Place collected material into corresponding 15 mL conical tubes.
Set a timer for 30 min to allow aggregates to sediment.
Aspirate supernatant carefully with a pipette or high-sensitivity aspirating pump after 30 min.
Ensure aggregates remain undisturbed at the bottom of 15 mL conical tube.
Resuspend aggregates in each 15 mL conical tube in 2 mL of vascular induction medium.
Place resuspended aggregates back into their respective wells on the 6-well plate.
Return plate to incubator (37 °C).
Gently pipette each well of aggregates up and down once per day using a 1 mL pipette.
Work on ice to prepare the desired final volume of ECM solution.
Pipette 500 µL of ECM into one well of a 12-well plate.
Ensure that no bubbles are formed and the well bottom and side meniscus are completely coated.
Place the plate back at 37 °C for 2 h.
Gather aggregates in the center of each well using a circular motion.
Use a 1 mL pipette to gently collect the aggregates and surrounding medium from each well.
Place the collected mixture into their corresponding 15 mL conical tubes.
Allow the aggregates to settle for 10-15 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Place the aggregates in the 15 mL conical tube on ice for 5 min.
Take the 12-well plate with the now polymerized layer 1 out of the incubator.
Resuspend aggregates in 500 µL of ECM.
Pipette ECM-aggregate suspension atop the already polymerized layer 1 using a 200 µL pipette tip.
Place the plate back at 37 °C for 2 h.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed (37 °C) sprouting medium to induce blood vessel differentiation.
Change the medium after 3 days and then every other day.
Work under sterile conditions to loosen the ECM sprouting matrix containing vascular networks using a rounded end of a sterile spatula.
Transfer the gel disk, including the vascular networks, to the lid of a 10 cm culture dish using sterile forceps.
Place the lid plus gel under a stereomicroscope adjusted to the desired magnification and focus.
Use sterile needles to cut out single blood vessel networks from the gel.
Transfer isolated organoids back into one well of an ultra-low attachment 6-well plate with 3 mL of sprouting medium.
Transfer single organoids from the 6-well plate to the wells of an ultra-low attachment 96-well plate using a 1 mL pipette.
Add 200 μL of pre-warmed (37 °C) sprouting medium to each well of the 96-well plate.
Check that organoids have a round and healthy morphology at 4-6 days post isolation in the 96-well plates.
Transfer organoids into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube using a cut 1 mL tip for fixation, blocking, and staining of the BVOs.
Use a pipette to remove remaining sprouting medium in the microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL of 4% PFA in PBS for 1 hour.
Wash fixed BVOs 3 times for 15 minutes each with 0.25% PBS-Tween.
Aspirate all 0.25% PBS-Tween after washing.
Permeabilize BVOs larger than 1 mm diameter with 1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 30-60 minutes at room temperature, if necessary.
Add 1 mL of blocking buffer to the newly fixed and permeabilized (if applicable) BVOs.
Remove the blocking buffer.
Add primary antibody diluted in 1 mL of blocking buffer at a ratio of 1:100.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C on an orbital shaker (12 rpm).
Remove the primary antibody solution.
Wash three times for 15 minutes each with 0.25% PBS-Tween.
Add secondary antibody and DAPI diluted in 1 mL of blocking buffer, secondary antibody at a ratio of 1:250 and DAPI at a ratio of 1:1000.
Incubate for 2 hours at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Remove the secondary antibody solution.
Wash three times for 15 minutes each with 0.25% PBS-Tween.
Mount spacers onto imaging coverslips as desired.
Transfer single organoids into spacer wells using a cut 1 mm pipette tip and 1 mL pipette.
Aspirate remaining PBS.
Fill the well with 150-200 µL of clearing solution heated to 75 °C, fully submerging the organoid.
Leave the organoids in a covered box in the dark at room temperature for 6 h to overnight if necessary.
Aspirate the clearing solution with a 100-200 µL pipette tip carefully.
Maneuver the organoid to the center of the spacer well gently.
Add drops of mounting gel warmed to 75 °C until the well is full.
Gently place the second coverslip on top of the mounting spacer to seal the samples.
Let the mounting gel cure in the dark at 4 °C overnight.
